purpose: Close report §2 kernel-time blind spot on the LIGHT contract (§2 is a light claim); reconcile the two denominators (per-PID process kernel% vs mpstat cpuset %sys+%soft).
findings: mpstat %sys+%soft (54.1/50.6/47.9%) reproduces report §2's 49-60% band (same cpuset wall-clock denominator as sar).

DENOMINATOR TRAP: exeris has the HIGHEST kernel fraction (54.1% mpstat) but the LOWEST absolute kernel-CPU/req (~38-40us) and lowest total CPU/req (57us). Lean user-space -> kernel is a bigger slice of a smaller pie. §2 must be stated per-request/absolute, not as a fraction.
Blind spot closed for light: per-PID kernel% + mpstat %sys+%soft + inline softirq all measured; no hidden ksoftirqd.
syscalls/req identical (~12.4) across all three at single-read; per-request kernel gap is per-syscall cost, not count.
Serialization negligible at light (0.8%); the Jackson question is heavy-only.

headline_39pct_reconciliation.note: At 1024m/4vcpu/256m/54k-rps the +39% kernel figure is not reproduced; closest match is total-CPU/req vs hibernate (+35%). Likely a different operating point (promotion light ~79k rps). Recommend restating §2 as absolute per-request with exact config.

loopback_caveat: Inline softirq attribution (worker/vert.x syscall context, no ksoftirqd) is a LOOPBACK property; on a real NIC RX softirq moves to ksoftirqd and per-PID misses it.
